source: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 7 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 7
knowledgePattern: Translate four real quartic roots into a full parameter interval
solution:
Put u=x2. The quadratic formula gives u=2±4−c. To give four distinct real values of x, these must be two different positive numbers.

They are real and different when c<4. The smaller value is positive when 2−4−c>0, which gives c>0. Therefore the exact condition is 0<c<4. At either endpoint, there are fewer than four distinct roots.

A necessary condition must contain every value in that interval. The only option that does is −1<c<5. It is not sufficient: for example, c=4 satisfies it but produces only two distinct real roots. Answer B.

hints.title: Turn the quartic into a quadratic
hints.body: Set u=x2. Rewrite the equation in u, remembering that u cannot be negative.
hints.recap: A positive value of x squared gives two real values of x.
hints.pitfall: If u is zero, those two values become the same.
hints.pause: What must be true of the quadratic’s roots to give four different x values?

recall.reminder: A positive value of x squared gives two real values of x.

hints.title: Check the two quadratic roots
hints.body: Use the quadratic formula for u. Require the square root in the formula to be real and nonzero, then require the smaller u value to be positive.
hints.recap: Two real roots are not enough here: both must be positive and different.
hints.pitfall: Check equality at each boundary before including it.
hints.pause: Find the exact interval of c values that works.

recall.reminder: Two real roots are not enough here: both must be positive and different.

hints.title: Compare the intervals
hints.body: A necessary condition must include every c value that works. To be not sufficient, it must also include a c value that fails.
hints.recap: Necessary means that every successful case satisfies the condition.
hints.pitfall: An interval that misses even one successful value is not necessary.
hints.pause: Draw your interval and the options on number lines, then compare them.
